description: Framework-agnostic headless rich text editor toolkit built on ProseMirror, with native Angular, React, Vue, and Vanilla components, Notion-style block UX, and a tree-shakeable extension model. MIT licensed. Full guides and API reference at https://domternal.dev/v1.
rules: The @domternal/core package is framework-agnostic and headless. Framework wrappers are @domternal/angular, @domternal/react, @domternal/vue, and @domternal/vanilla.

Import editor primitives and built-in extensions from @domternal/core. Optional features are separate @domternal/extension-* packages: table, image, math, emoji, mention, markdown, paste-cleanup, block-controls, toc, details, code-block-lowlight.
Use StarterKit for a batteries-included schema; wire Document/Text/Paragraph and marks by hand only for a minimal headless setup.
Notion-style block UX (slash menu, drag-to-reorder, block context menu, smart paste) comes from @domternal/extension-block-controls.
Styling is opt-in via @domternal/theme (CSS custom properties) and is separate from the headless core.
JavaScript extension exports are tree-shakeable: import and register only what you use. The optional @domternal/theme package ships one complete CSS stylesheet.

Domternal Free is the current set of 18 MIT-licensed @domternal workspace packages, including extension-paste-cleanup, introduced in 1.3.0. Domternal Pro is a separate commercially licensed suite distributed through public npm with a private source repository.

The @domternal/extension-paste-cleanup package is opt-in and introduces Office HTML paste normalization in 1.3.0, with preserve/adapt formatting, bounded localized feedback, and a standalone /html helper. It is not part of StarterKit or wrapper defaults and does not import DOCX files. A historical reviewed native baseline qualifies Word 16.113.3 for Mac copied in Safari 26.5.2, Chrome 154 and Firefox 155, and Google Docs web copied in Chrome 153 on macOS, replayed through synthetic paste events. Current committed English fixtures are authored synthetic derivatives, not new native captures. Google Docs in Safari and Firefox, Word for Windows, Word on the web, LibreOffice and Collabora remain unqualified; complete Word fidelity is not claimed. DOCX file import is available separately through @domternal-pro/extension-import, in the independently versioned Pro suite.

Upgrade installed @domternal/* packages together to 1.6.0. Domternal peer ranges are >=1.6.0 <2.0.0; Core 1.6.0 requires @domternal/pm >=1.6.0 <2.0.0 at runtime. The 1.5.1 patch fixed PasteCleanup image byte accounting and configuration guidance. Keep the 1.3.0 migration notes and 1.3.1 compatibility fixes in mind when upgrading older applications: JSON loading normalizes unsupported attributes and refused links, schema validation is stricter, and transaction callbacks include appended changes. The 1.3.1 patch restored compatibility defaults without reverting every 1.3 behavior change. Observe onContentDiagnostic, use normalizeContent for external JSON consumers, and follow the Core README before migrating a shared document with normalizeContentAttributes.

Core and theme 1.4.0 support opt-in TextColor.configure({ contrast: 'auto' }). It adjusts opaque literal colors below 4.5:1 on supported known backgrounds in the live editor; the default is original. Stored content, serialized HTML, clipboard output, export and print preserve authored colors. Unsupported or uncertain paint remains unchanged. Use matching Core and theme packages, or the documented custom screen styles.

Core 1.4.0 message definitions can declare optionalTranslation: true. CompleteMessages keeps unmarked definitions required and checks message IDs and callback parameters; optional definitions may use the built-in fallback. Required<CompleteMessages<typeof messages>> requires translations for every current definition. Runtime i18n.messages remains partial.

Free 1.5.0 introduced the optional ListLabels extension and the pure @domternal/core/list-labels entry for literal Unicode bullets and single native ordered counters with bounded prefixes and suffixes. Free 1.6.0 adds bounded compound templates derived from actual list ancestry and local static 8-bit RGB/RGBA PNG markers up to 32 by 32 pixels and 4 KiB, with readable text fallback. ListLabel, readListLabel, formatListLabel and getNodeListLabel retain their counter/text contract; use ExtendedListLabel, readExtendedListLabel, parseExtendedListLabel, formatExtendedListLabel and getNodeExtendedListLabel for the added variants. The node readers are available only from the main Core entry. ListLabels is not part of StarterKit; existing schemas stay unchanged without it. All collaborative writers must enable the same schema. Standalone HTML needs getListLabelStyleSheet and must be regenerated after structural edits. Canonical editor metadata support does not imply general Word compound-numbering or picture-bullet recognition.

Free 1.6.0 adds Image.configure({ enableTransforms: true }) in @domternal/extension-image for non-destructive crop, rotation and mirroring. It adds the imageTransform attribute and setImageTransform command while keeping source bytes unchanged. The option is false by default, ordinary Image schema/JSON stay unchanged, and the default menu gains no transform controls. Enable the option on every collaborative writer before storing geometry.

Free 1.6.0 adds opt-in DocumentNotes from @domternal/core for editable footnote/endnote bodies and references in ordinary editor JSON, including navigation, repeated references, custom labels and undo. It is not part of StarterKit or a paginated footnote editor. Free 1.6.0 also adds opt-in TableLayout beside Table for bounded row heights, cell padding/borders and page-break preferences. It adds commands but no settings panel. Enable each corresponding schema on every collaborative writer. Pro Import/Export support for these new models belongs to a separate upcoming Pro release; this Free release does not publish those DOCX/PDF adapters.

Free 1.6.0 adds createSchema(extensions) for headless and worker pipelines using the editor's extension configuration. It creates no view, plugins or editor lifecycle and does not normalize JSON. Print.configure({ prepareResources: true }) optionally waits for live images and fonts before command-driven printing; the default stays immediate. cancelPrintPreparation and the optional storage.print.preparation promise expose cancellation and completion. Matching Core, Table and theme support eligible multirow print headers without changing document JSON or selection. Native browser printing cannot wait for asynchronous preparation, and browser pagination still applies.

Free 1.5.0 PasteCleanup retains supported Word typography from bounded simple stylesheet selectors and full-width paragraph or heading fills with BlockColor. formattingForPaste can choose preserve or adapt once per paste before asynchronous image preparation; it does not expose clipboard content. Supported first-paragraph formatting is kept in an empty paragraph destination. Actual-value probes and bounded post-insertion tracking report uncertainty or confirmed loss without claiming full source fidelity. Matching theme styles provide localized image upload feedback and readable default text on known block backgrounds.

Domternal Pro runs in customer-chosen infrastructure and requires no Domternal-operated editor cloud. Current product, pricing, and licensing facts live at https://domternal.dev/pro/, https://domternal.dev/free-vs-pro/, and https://domternal.dev/license-explained/.
Full guides, per-extension API, and the changelog live at https://domternal.dev/v1.
